ruleName: Taking Relief from Abnormal Course Conditions
title: What if the nearest point is in a bad lie?
question: If the nearest point of complete relief is in thick rough, a bush, or on a steep slope, what are your options?

choices.text: You can take relief and play from there, even if it's a difficult shot.
You may ignore the rules and choose any spot you like.
You can decide to play the ball as it lies without taking relief.
You can move your ball to the green for an easier shot.

explanation: You can either take relief at the correct relief point, even if the lie is poor, or you may play the ball as it lies and not take relief.

juniorVersion.title: What if your free drop puts you in a tricky spot?
juniorVersion.question: If your nearest place to drop the ball is in long grass, in a bush, or on a steep hill, what can you do?

choices.text: You can drop and play the ball from there, even if it’s a hard place to hit from.
You can forget the rules and put your ball anywhere you want.
You can choose to just hit your ball from where it is now, without moving it.
You can move your ball onto the green to make it easier.

juniorVersion.explanation: You must either drop at the nearest spot, even if it’s not easy, or just play your ball the way it is. You can’t pick any spot you like.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A special rule that lets you move your ball away from things like puddles or paths.
The closest place where you are not standing on the thing you get relief from.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children how sometimes the right place to drop means a harder shot. Let them try dropping near rough or bushes safely.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think they can always put the ball in a nice spot.
Children may think they can move the ball to the green or choose any place after taking relief.
